title: Female Reproductive System
content:
# Female Reproductive System

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Identify the main structures of the female reproductive system
- Describe the functions of each structure
- Explain how eggs are produced and released
- Describe the structure and function of egg cells

## Introduction

The **female reproductive system** produces eggs (female gametes), receives sperm, provides a site for fertilisation, and supports the development of a baby during pregnancy. Understanding this system is essential for understanding human reproduction.

## Key Concepts

### Overview of Female Reproductive System

**Main functions:**
- Produce eggs (female gametes)
- Produce female hormones
- Receive sperm
- Site of fertilisation
- Support embryo/fetal development

[DIAGRAM: Female reproductive system showing all structures]

### Structures and Functions

| Structure | Function |
|-----------|----------|
| Ovaries | Produce eggs and hormones |
| Oviduct (Fallopian tube) | Site of fertilisation; transports egg |
| Uterus | Where embryo implants and develops |
| Cervix | Entrance to uterus; produces mucus |
| Vagina | Receives sperm; birth canal |

### The Ovaries

**Structure:**
- Pair of organs
- Located in lower abdomen
- Contain follicles (developing eggs)
- About 3-4 cm long

**Functions:**
1. Produce eggs (oogenesis)
2. Produce hormones (oestrogen, progesterone)

**Key points:**
- Girls born with all eggs (~1-2 million)
- Only ~400 released during lifetime
- Usually one egg released per month

### Egg Production (Oogenesis)

**Process:**
1. Eggs begin development before birth
2. Development pauses until puberty
3. Each month, follicles develop
4. Usually one egg matures fully
5. Ovulation releases the egg

**Timing:**
- Begins: before birth
- Pauses: at birth (primary oocyte stage)
- Resumes: at puberty
- Ends: at menopause (~45-55 years)

### Egg (Ovum) Structure

| Part | Function |
|------|----------|
| Nucleus | Contains genetic material (haploid) |
| Cytoplasm | Contains nutrients for early development |
| Cell membrane | Controls what enters/exits |
| Zona pellucida | Protective layer; sperm recognition |
| Corona radiata | Layer of follicle cells; protection |

[DIAGRAM: Structure of an egg cell]

### Comparing Egg and Sperm

| Feature | Egg | Sperm |
|---------|-----|-------|
| Size | Large (~0.1 mm) | Small (~0.05 mm) |
| Mobility | Immobile | Mobile (flagellum) |
| Cytoplasm | Lots (nutrients) | Little |
| Number | One per month | Millions daily |
| Produced | Before birth | From puberty |
| Haploid | Yes | Yes |

### The Oviducts (Fallopian Tubes)

**Structure:**
- Two tubes connecting ovaries to uterus
- ~10-12 cm long
- Lined with cilia and muscle
- Funnel-shaped end near ovary (fimbriae)

**Functions:**
1. Collect egg after ovulation (fimbriae)
2. Site of fertilisation
3. Transport fertilised egg to uterus

**How egg moves:**
- Cilia beat to waft egg along
- Muscle contractions (peristalsis)
- Takes ~4-5 days to reach uterus

### The Uterus (Womb)

**Structure:**
- Pear-shaped muscular organ
- Thick muscular wall (myometrium)
- Inner lining (endometrium)
- Highly elastic

**Functions:**
1. Site of implantation
2. Nourishes developing embryo/fetus
3. Protects developing baby
4. Contracts during birth

**The endometrium:**
- Rich blood supply
- Thickens each month
- Embryo implants here
- Shed during menstruation if no pregnancy

### The Cervix

**Structure:**
- Neck of uterus
- Opens into vagina
- Has a small opening (os)

**Functions:**
- Produces mucus
- Mucus changes during cycle
- Thins at ovulation (allows sperm through)
- Seals uterus during pregnancy
- Dilates during birth

### The Vagina

**Structure:**
- Muscular tube
- ~10 cm long
- Highly elastic
- Acidic environment

**Functions:**
- Receives penis and sperm during intercourse
- Birth canal
- Passage for menstrual flow

### Female Hormones

| Hormone | Produced by | Functions |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| Oestrogen | Ovaries | Secondary sexual characteristics; thickens endometrium |
| Progesterone | Ovaries (corpus luteum) | Maintains endometrium; supports pregnancy |
| FSH | Pituitary | Stimulates follicle development |
| LH | Pituitary | Triggers ovulation |

### Secondary Sexual Characteristics

**Triggered by oestrogen at puberty:**
- Breast development
- Widening of hips
- Growth of pubic and underarm hair
- Beginning of menstrual cycle
- Fat deposition (hips, thighs)

### The Menstrual Cycle Overview

| Day | Event |
|-----|-------|
| 1-5 | Menstruation (lining shed) |
| 6-13 | Follicle develops; lining rebuilds |
| 14 | Ovulation (egg released) |
| 15-28 | Lining maintained by progesterone |
| 28/1 | If no pregnancy, cycle restarts |

[DIAGRAM: Overview of menstrual cycle events]

## Common Exam Questions

- Name the parts of the female reproductive system
- Describe the function of the ovaries
- Compare egg and sperm cells
- Explain the role of the oviduct in fertilisation

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** Women produce new eggs throughout life
- **Reality:** Women are born with all their eggs

- **Misconception:** Ovulation occurs on day 14 for all women
- **Reality:** Timing varies between individuals and cycles

- **Misconception:** Both ovaries release an egg each month
- **Reality:** Usually only one ovary releases an egg

- **Misconception:** The uterus is where fertilisation occurs
- **Reality:** Fertilisation usually occurs in the oviduct

## Practice Questions

1. Name the organ that produces eggs. (1 mark)

2. State the function of the oviduct. (2 marks)

3. Describe two differences between egg cells and sperm cells. (2 marks)

4. Explain the role of the endometrium in reproduction. (3 marks)

5. Describe the structure and function of the ovary. (4 marks)

6. Compare the structure of an egg cell with a sperm cell. Explain how each is adapted for its function. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Ovary | Female gonad; produces eggs and hormones |
| Oviduct | Tube connecting ovary to uterus; site of fertilisation |
| Uterus | Organ where embryo develops |
| Cervix | Neck of uterus |
| Vagina | Receives sperm; birth canal |
| Ovulation | Release of egg from ovary |
| Endometrium | Lining of uterus |
| Oestrogen | Female sex hormone |
| Oogenesis | Process of egg production |

## Summary

- Ovaries produce eggs and hormones (oestrogen, progesterone)
- Women are born with all their eggs (~1-2 million)
- Eggs are large, immobile, and contain nutrients
- Oviducts are the site of fertilisation
- Cilia and muscles move egg towards uterus
- Uterus is where embryo implants and develops
- Endometrium is shed during menstruation if no pregnancy
- Oestrogen triggers female secondary sexual characteristics
